title: Direct Knowledge Of Allah 19th Degree 2nd Truth Divine Speech

questions.question: What is the main topic introduced at the beginning of the target passage?
questions.answer: Divine speech as a truth that comes from the attribute of Speech.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does the Qur'anic verse about the sea becoming ink suggest about Divine speech?
questions.answer: It suggests that Divine speech has no limit.

questions.question: In the passage, what is presented as the clearest sign that a being exists?
questions.answer: Speech.

questions.question: Why does the passage treat Divine speech as a very strong proof?
questions.answer: Because speech shows the existence of the speaker, so Divine speech points to Allah’s existence and oneness.

questions.question: Which two major evidences of this truth are named first?
questions.answer: Revelation and inspiration.

questions.question: What other kind of evidence is said to support this truth besides revelation and inspiration?
questions.answer: Sacred and heavenly books.

questions.question: Which book is described as the brightest and most comprehensive proof?
questions.answer: The Qur'an.

questions.question: Why does the passage not explain this truth in full detail here?
questions.answer: Because those explanations were already given in other sections, so the reader is referred there instead.

questions.question: How is the verse about the sea and ink used in this section?
questions.answer: As a lofty sign that expresses the endlessness of Divine words and adds its witness to the earlier proofs.

questions.question: Who else is mentioned as bearing witness together with Allah in the quoted verse?
questions.answer: The angels and people of knowledge.

questions.question: What central belief is affirmed repeatedly in the quoted Qur'anic testimony?
questions.answer: That no one deserves worship except Allah.

questions.question: What two Divine qualities are named at the end of that verse?
questions.answer: Might and wisdom.

questions.question: In the summary of the traveler’s lesson, how is Allah described in relation to existence?
questions.answer: As necessarily existent.

questions.question: In that same summary, how is Allah described in relation to unity?
questions.answer: As One and Unique.

questions.question: What does the passage say belongs to Allah in terms of names and attributes?
questions.answer: The most beautiful names, the highest attributes, and the most exalted likeness.

questions.question: What points to Allah’s necessary existence in unity according to the passage?
questions.answer: His necessarily existent essence together with the agreement of His sacred attributes, beautiful names, qualities, and acts.

questions.question: What general pattern in Divine action is mentioned as a witness to this truth?
questions.answer: A continuous ruling activity shown through bringing things into existence, creating, making, and originating.

questions.question: Which qualities are linked with acts like bringing into being and creating?
questions.answer: Will and power.

questions.question: Which qualities are linked with determining, shaping, and regulating?
questions.answer: Choice and wisdom.

questions.question: Which qualities are linked with ordering, preserving, managing, and nurturing?
questions.answer: Purpose and mercy.

questions.question: What do complete order and balance add to the argument?
questions.answer: They strengthen the testimony that these acts come from one wise and just Lord.

questions.question: In the note, what is said about the truths in the nineteen degrees of the first chapter?
questions.answer: They prove necessary existence through existence and presence, and also show unity through their comprehensiveness.

questions.question: Why were those truths treated first as proofs of necessary existence?
questions.answer: Because they show existence more openly and directly.

questions.question: How will the truths in the second chapter be treated differently?
questions.answer: They will be presented mainly as proofs of Divine unity, while necessity will be implied.

questions.question: What mutual relationship between unity and necessity does the note teach?
questions.answer: Each one proves the other.

questions.question: What wording change is mentioned between the first and second chapters?
questions.answer: The first stresses testimony, while the second stresses witnessing to indicate the clearer visibility of Divine unity.

questions.question: Why does the writer say the second chapter will be brief?
questions.answer: Because various obstacles prevented a fuller explanation.

questions.question: Where does the writer direct readers for fuller explanation of these matters?
questions.answer: To other parts of the Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: What attribute is the source of Divine discourse in the passage?
questions.answer: The attribute of Speech.

questions.question: What does the cited verse teach about the amount of Divine words?
questions.answer: They are beyond measure and never exhausted.

questions.question: What humanly understandable sign is used to argue for the existence of a speaker?
questions.answer: The fact that speech reveals the one who speaks.

questions.question: Based on that reasoning, what does Divine discourse prove about Allah?
questions.answer: His existence and His oneness.

questions.question: What two forms of communication from Allah are named as strong supports for this truth?
questions.answer: Revelation and inspiration.

questions.question: What written sources are also counted as evidence?
questions.answer: Sacred and heavenly books.

questions.question: Among those books, which one is singled out in a special way?
questions.answer: The Qur'an, as the most brilliant and all-encompassing proof.

questions.question: What does the passage imply by sending readers to other degrees of the treatise?
questions.answer: That this truth has already been established with broader arguments elsewhere.

questions.question: In the verse from Surah Al 'Imran, who joins in testifying besides Allah?
questions.answer: The angels and those who possess knowledge.

questions.question: What does their shared witness emphasize?
questions.answer: The absolute oneness of Allah.

questions.question: What moral quality is mentioned in connection with this testimony?
questions.answer: Justice or upright fairness.

questions.question: In the summarized declaration, what titles are used to stress Allah’s uniqueness?
questions.answer: The Necessary Existent, the One, and the Unique.

questions.question: How does the passage connect Allah’s names and attributes to the proof of His existence?
questions.answer: Their complete agreement points to the reality of the One to whom they belong.

questions.question: What does the agreement of Divine qualities and acts show?
questions.answer: That they come from one Lord, not many separate powers.

questions.question: What larger reality is said to appear through the manifestation of dominicality?
questions.answer: The self-disclosure of Divinity.

questions.question: What kinds of acts are listed as signs of ongoing Divine activity?
questions.answer: Giving existence, creating, making, originating, determining, shaping, regulating, preserving, administering, and nurturing.

questions.question: What does the pairing of action with will and power suggest?
questions.answer: That creation is intentional and fully controlled.

questions.question: What does the pairing of regulation with wisdom suggest?
questions.answer: That the universe is arranged with insight and purpose.

questions.question: What does the pairing of nurture with mercy suggest?
questions.answer: That care for creation is compassionate, not random.

questions.question: How do order and balance function in the argument of the passage?
questions.answer: They act as visible signs that support belief in Divine unity.

questions.question: What does the note say the nineteen degrees in the first chapter do beyond proving existence?
questions.answer: They also testify to Allah’s unity and oneness through their comprehensiveness.

questions.question: Why were they classified first under necessary existence rather than unity?
questions.answer: Because their clearest and most explicit force was in establishing existence.

questions.question: How will the same kinds of truths function in the second chapter?
questions.answer: As direct proofs of unity and indirect proofs of necessity.

questions.question: What is the logical link between necessity and unity in the note?
questions.answer: Neither stands alone; each confirms the other.

questions.question: Why does the writer mention a repeated difference in phrasing between the two chapters?
questions.answer: To mark the shift in focus from establishing existence to highlighting visible unity.

questions.question: What does that shift in phrasing suggest about unity?
questions.answer: That unity is being treated as something especially evident and observable in the signs.

questions.question: What practical limitation affected the treatment of the second chapter?
questions.answer: The writer faced obstacles and therefore had to be concise.

questions.question: What truth is being discussed under “the second truth” in the target passage?
questions.answer: The truth of Divine discourse.

questions.question: From which Divine attribute does this discourse come?
questions.answer: From Speech.

questions.question: What image from the Qur'an is used to show the boundlessness of Divine words?
questions.answer: The idea that even a sea turned into ink would not be enough.

questions.question: What basic principle about speech and existence is stated in the passage?
questions.answer: Speech is the clearest indicator that a speaker exists.

questions.question: What theological conclusion is drawn from that principle?
questions.answer: Divine discourse is an endless proof that Allah exists and is One.

questions.question: Name one reason the passage gives for not expanding the discussion at length in this place.
questions.answer: The topic had already been explained and confirmed in earlier degrees of the work.

questions.question: What are the first two evidences named for this truth?
questions.answer: Revelation and inspiration.

questions.question: What broader written evidence is added after those two?
questions.answer: Holy and heavenly books.

questions.question: What makes the Qur'an stand out among those evidences in the passage?
questions.answer: It is described as especially radiant and comprehensive.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the role of the cited verse itself?
questions.answer: It offers its own witness while supporting the previous testimonies.

questions.question: What verse is then quoted to sum up the traveler’s lesson at that station?
questions.answer: The verse declaring that Allah testifies, along with angels and people of knowledge, that there is no god but Him.

questions.question: What shared testimony appears in that verse?
questions.answer: The affirmation of Allah’s sole divinity.

questions.question: Which two groups besides Allah are mentioned as witnesses?
questions.answer: Angels and those who have knowledge.

questions.question: How is Allah described in the declaration that follows the verse?
questions.answer: As necessarily existent, one, and uniquely one.

questions.question: What three categories belonging to Allah are highlighted there?
questions.answer: His beautiful names, supreme attributes, and highest likeness.

questions.question: What does the agreement of all sacred attributes and beautiful names point to?
questions.answer: The necessary existence and unity of the Divine Essence.

questions.question: Why does the passage list many Divine acts one after another?
questions.answer: To show the wide scope and consistency of Divine rule and action.

questions.question: What is shown by acts such as creating and originating being tied to will and power?
questions.answer: That existence comes from deliberate and capable action.

questions.question: What is shown by acts such as determining and regulating being tied to choice and wisdom?
questions.answer: That the order of creation is selected intelligently, not blindly.

questions.question: What is shown by acts such as preserving and nurturing being tied to purpose and mercy?
questions.answer: That care for creation is meaningful and compassionate.

questions.question: In the note, what did the truths of the first chapter primarily establish?
questions.answer: Necessary existence.

questions.question: What did those same truths also establish, though less directly in the arrangement?
questions.answer: Divine unity and oneness.

questions.question: What will be the main emphasis in the second chapter?
questions.answer: Proofs of Divine unity.

questions.question: What will remain implied even when unity is emphasized?
questions.answer: Necessary existence.

questions.question: What reciprocal relationship is stated between unity and necessity?
questions.answer: Unity points to necessity, and necessity points to unity.

questions.question: How does the passage resolve that lack of full explanation?
questions.answer: By referring readers to other parts of the Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: What subject opens the marked passage?
questions.answer: Divine speech.

questions.question: How is Divine speech connected to one of Allah’s attributes?
questions.answer: It is presented as flowing from the attribute of Speech.

questions.question: What does the passage infer from the Qur'anic image of the sea as ink?
questions.answer: Allah’s words cannot be exhausted.

questions.question: What everyday logic underlies the statement that speech proves existence?
questions.answer: If there is speech, there must be a speaker.

questions.question: What two major realities does Divine discourse testify to?
questions.answer: Allah’s existence and His unity.

questions.question: Which two evidences are said to have already explained this truth in earlier sections?
questions.answer: Revelation and inspiration.

questions.question: What additional category of proof comes from transmitted writings?
questions.answer: Sacred and heavenly books.

questions.question: Why is the Qur'an given a special place among those writings?
questions.answer: Because it is presented as the most shining and comprehensive proof.

questions.question: What function do the “lights and mysteries” of the verse serve?
questions.answer: They provide enough insight to confirm the truth without a longer explanation.

questions.question: In the next quoted verse, what does Allah Himself declare?
questions.answer: That no deity exists except Him.

questions.question: Who supports this declaration according to the same verse?
questions.answer: Angels and possessors of knowledge.

questions.question: What does the inclusion of angels and learned people add to the meaning?
questions.answer: It shows a wide and noble agreement in bearing witness to tawhid.

questions.question: What does “steadfast in equity” contribute to the picture of Allah in the verse?
questions.answer: It shows that His rule and witness are joined with perfect justice.

questions.question: In the later declaration, what expression points to Allah’s necessary existence?
questions.answer: The title that describes Him as the One whose existence is necessary.

questions.question: What expression in that declaration points to exclusiveness in unity?
questions.answer: The titles that describe Him as one and utterly unique.

questions.question: How do Allah’s names and attributes function in the argument?
questions.answer: Their total harmony points back to the single Divine Essence.

questions.question: What is the significance of mentioning dominant qualities and deeds together?
questions.answer: It shows that both what Allah is like and what Allah does agree in affirming oneness.

questions.question: What broad truth is said to appear through dominicality?
questions.answer: The self-manifestation of Divinity.

questions.question: Why are so many creative and governing acts listed in sequence?
questions.answer: To show the continuity, reach, and unity of Divine action across all things.

questions.question: What is the effect of linking these acts with will, power, wisdom, purpose, and mercy?
questions.answer: It presents creation as intentional, skillful, wise, and compassionate.

questions.question: What do complete order and equilibrium indicate in the passage?
questions.answer: They serve as visible evidence that these acts come from one perfectly governing Lord.

questions.question: According to the note, what was the main role of the truths in the first chapter?
questions.answer: They were mainly used to prove necessary existence.

questions.question: What was their secondary role?
questions.answer: They also proved unity and oneness.

questions.question: How will the second chapter rearrange that emphasis?
questions.answer: It will make unity the direct focus and necessity the indirect one.

questions.question: What statement in the note shows that these two doctrines are inseparable?
questions.answer: The note says each one proves the other.

questions.question: Why is a change in repeated wording important in the structure of the work?
questions.answer: It signals a shift in what is being highlighted in the argument.

questions.question: What prevented the writer from giving a full commentary on the second chapter here?
questions.answer: Various obstacles forced him to keep it short.

questions.question: What truth does the marked passage begin by naming?
questions.answer: Divine discourse.

questions.question: What Divine attribute is identified as its source?
questions.answer: Speech.

questions.question: What does the cited Qur'anic image teach about the quantity of Divine words?
questions.answer: They are limitless.

questions.question: What sign of existence is called the clearest in the passage?
questions.answer: Speech.

questions.question: How does that idea become an argument for faith?
questions.answer: If speech proves a speaker, then Divine speech proves Allah’s existence and unity.

questions.question: What two forms of Divine communication are named as strong evidence for this?
questions.answer: Revelation and inspiration.

questions.question: What written evidence beyond those two is mentioned?
questions.answer: Sacred and heavenly scriptures.

questions.question: Which scripture is presented as the strongest broad proof here?
questions.answer: The Qur'an.

questions.question: Why does the writer choose not to repeat all those discussions in this passage?
questions.answer: Because they were already explained in earlier degrees of the treatise.

questions.question: What is the core message of the verse from Surah Al 'Imran included here?
questions.answer: Allah alone is truly divine.

questions.question: Who are mentioned as witnesses alongside Allah in that verse?
questions.answer: Angels and those who have knowledge.

questions.question: What does the presence of knowledgeable people among the witnesses imply?
questions.answer: Sound knowledge supports belief in Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What does the verse say about Allah’s rule besides affirming His oneness?
questions.answer: It presents Him as acting with justice.

questions.question: In the declaration that follows, how is Allah described regarding His names and attributes?
questions.answer: He possesses the beautiful names and the highest attributes.

questions.question: What does the declaration say about Allah’s likeness or exemplar?
questions.answer: That the highest and most exalted similitude belongs to Him.

questions.question: What points to Allah’s necessary existence in unity according to that statement?
questions.answer: His necessarily existent essence together with the unanimous witness of His attributes, names, qualities, and acts.

questions.question: Why is consensus language used repeatedly in that declaration?
questions.answer: To show that every Divine sign agrees without conflict in pointing to the same truth.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the manifestation of Divinity within dominicality?
questions.answer: It appears in the greatness and continuity of Divine activity.

questions.question: Which acts are associated with will and power?
questions.answer: Bringing into existence, creating, making, and originating.

questions.question: Which acts are associated with choice and wisdom?
questions.answer: Determining, shaping, regulating, and turning affairs.

questions.question: Which acts are associated with purpose and mercy?
questions.answer: Disposing, organizing, preserving, administering, and sustaining.

questions.question: What do order and balance contribute to the passage’s reasoning?
questions.answer: They confirm that these actions belong to one wise and merciful Lord.

questions.question: In the note, how are the truths of the first chapter said to prove necessary existence?
questions.answer: Through existence and presence.

questions.question: How are they said to prove unity?
questions.answer: Through their comprehensiveness.

questions.question: Why were they first counted under necessary existence?
questions.answer: Because that aspect was more direct and obvious.

questions.question: How will the truths in the second chapter be designated?
questions.answer: As proofs of Divine unity that also imply necessity.

questions.question: What final reason is given for the brief treatment here?
questions.answer: The writer was constrained by obstacles and left fuller explanation to other parts of the work.

questions.question: What specific truth is announced at the start of the target passage?
questions.answer: The truth of Divine discourse.

questions.question: From which attribute does this discourse proceed?
questions.answer: From the attribute of Speech.

questions.question: What does the verse about the sea becoming ink communicate about Allah’s words?
questions.answer: They are endless.

questions.question: What proof from ordinary experience does the passage use to support its claim?
questions.answer: A being’s speech clearly shows that the being exists.

questions.question: When that principle is applied to Allah, what two conclusions follow?
questions.answer: That Allah exists and that He is one.

questions.question: What two evidences are said to have been discussed elsewhere in the treatise?
questions.answer: Revelation and inspiration.

questions.question: What additional textual proof is mentioned besides those two?
questions.answer: Heavenly and sacred books.

questions.question: Which of those books is described in the most exalted terms?
questions.answer: The Qur'an.

questions.question: What teaching method is used here instead of repeating detailed proofs?
questions.answer: The reader is directed to earlier sections, and only a brief reminder is given.

questions.question: What key doctrine is stated in the verse from Surah Al 'Imran?
questions.answer: There is no god except Allah.

questions.question: Which two groups are mentioned with Allah as witnesses?
questions.answer: Angels and those who possess knowledge.

questions.question: What quality of Allah’s governance is highlighted in that verse?
questions.answer: Perfect justice.

questions.question: In the lesson summary, what title shows that Allah depends on no one for existence?
questions.answer: The title indicating necessary existence.

questions.question: What titles stress that Allah has no partner or equal in His being?
questions.answer: The titles of oneness and uniqueness.

questions.question: What possessions of Allah are named right after those titles?
questions.answer: His beautiful names, supreme attributes, and highest similitude.

questions.question: What does the passage say collectively points to Allah’s necessary existence in unity?
questions.answer: The agreement of His essence, attributes, names, qualities, and acts.

questions.question: How does the passage portray Divine activity in the world?
questions.answer: As continuous, commanding, and expressed through many forms of creating and governing.

questions.question: What does linking creation with will and power teach?
questions.answer: That creation is deliberate and fully able to be carried out.

questions.question: What does linking regulation with choice and wisdom teach?
questions.answer: That the arrangement of things is selected and wise.

questions.question: What does linking nurture and administration with purpose and mercy teach?
questions.answer: That Divine care has meaning, aim, and compassion.

questions.question: What role do order and equilibrium play in the argument?
questions.answer: They are signs that the whole system is governed by one just and wise Lord.

questions.question: In the explanatory note, what were the nineteen degrees above mainly treated as?
questions.answer: Proofs of necessary existence.

questions.question: What else did those same truths also attest?
questions.answer: Allah’s unity and oneness.

questions.question: How will the second chapter classify similar truths?
questions.answer: As proofs of unity in an explicit way and of necessity in an implied way.

questions.question: What doctrinal relationship does the note state between unity and necessity?
questions.answer: Each serves as evidence for the other.

questions.question: Why did the writer not explain the second chapter degree by degree in full?
questions.answer: He was prevented by different obstacles and had to summarize.
